Ownership. Reuse. Execution.

UML class and object models, activity flows, and runtime sequences. Follow one relationship at a time: what owns an item, what refers to a shared definition, and what executes when an event occurs.

Start with containment ↓

How to read these models

These are conceptual UML models of documented behavior, not a dump of Emerson’s internal classes or an SDK. Names such as GraphicElement and PropertyValue express concepts; they are not asserted programming identifiers. Each diagram states whether it is a type model, an example object model, or an execution flow.

OwnerPart
Composition / ownership

The diamond sits at the owner. It identifies contained configuration, not a reference to a separate reusable definition.

ConsumerDefinition
Navigable association

The consumer refers to another item. Referencing does not make that item its child.

ClientSupplier
Dependency / named usage

Read the label: uses, calls or creates a copy. Ongoing GEM class references are solid associations in the object model.

SpecificGeneral
Generalization

The hollow triangle points to the more general conceptual type. A nested GEM is composition, not inheritance.

Multiplicity: 1 exactly one; 0..1 optional single; 0..* zero or more. {xor} marks alternative ownership paths. Underlined name : Type means an example object. In sequences, time flows downward; in activities, arrows show processing order. Teal = graphic objects; purple = shared definitions / workspace; magenta = values / code.

01 / TYPE MODELS

What can own what?

Start with saved configuration and its contained elements. Explorer panes, the Palette and property editors are tools for manipulating this structure; they are not additional runtime ownership layers.

DeltaV Live · Graphics Studio
DeltaV Operate · Configure / Run

Live placement and editing rules

Owner / destinationWhat belongs thereRestriction that matters
Configuration libraryGEM classes, templates, standards, functionsLibrary items are definitions. A folder is organization, not a data type.
Display / contextual displaySupported graphic elements, groups, GEM instances; variables and interactionsPalette choices depend on the active configuration. A contextual display is not embedded merely because a button opens it.
GEM classElement tree, nested GEM instances, exposed custom properties, variables and interactionsEdit the class to change shared structure or interactions.
Unlinked GEMElements, groups, linked or unlinked nested GEMs; own custom propertiesCan add content locally. Nested GEM links can remain even though the outer GEM is unlinked.
Linked GEM instanceClass-defined content + instance property values + eligible overridesAn override cannot add/remove elements or add/remove/change nested animations. Interactions are edited on the class.
GroupMember elements; local variables and supported behaviorGrouping provides local composition. It does not create a reusable GEM class or a GEM Configuration Designer.
LayoutScreen/frame arrangement; configuration-specific graphics, variables and interactionsUse its context-specific Palette. Do not assume every control is legal in every container.
Tab / textTab → tab items; text → its data placeholdersThese are owned UI substructures, not Library Explorer categories.

Palette is the placement catalog.

Your sketch correctly includes shapes, data, batch and user-entry elements as well as GEM classes. The active document determines the catalog. The saved configuration contains the placed result.

02 / WORKED OBJECT EXAMPLE

Worked example: two pumps sharing a definition

This applies the types and ownership rules in Section 1 to named objects: AreaA, P101 and P102. It adds the reuse relationships: both Live pumps reference one definition, which itself uses a nested component. The Operate example distinguishes source dynamos, placed copies and shared code. These are illustrative objects, not your plant configuration.

What happens when you change something?

Change / operationLive behaviorOperate comparison
Save a GEM class editUpdates linked instances in configuration; affected containing displays must be published for online use. The class itself is not published.Do not infer identical propagation from placement of a dynamo. Inspect the particular updater or engineering routine.
Change one exposed instance propertyChanges that placement’s input/settings. Child properties use it only where they reference it.A dynamo edit form may run VBA that changes many child properties on that placement.
Override an eligible linked child propertyThat property stops tracking the class value until the override is removed. Other class links remain.A local object edit is not evidence of a tracked Live-style override.
Unlink an outer GEMKeeps the configuration at unlinking; stops its own class updates. Child GEM links may remain.A source copy and a placed object must still be assessed separately.
Drag / Alt-drag / Shift+Alt-dragWhere linked creation is permitted: linked / outer unlinked with nested links retained / outer and nested GEMs unlinked.Operate placement has its own associated-code and dependency-copy rules.
Use a display or layout templateCreates an initial document. There is no ongoing template-class inheritance; nested GEM links are a separate matter.A starter picture supplies initial content; subsequent update scripts are separate behavior.

03 / EXPOSED OPTIONS & THEIR EFFECTS

Which options does an object expose, and what uses them?

A configuration contract means the interface offered to whoever configures the object: option names, types, defaults, constraints and intended effects. It is an explanatory term here, not a separate DeltaV component.

For example, a Boolean option named EUVisibility is useful only if the units label’s Visible property consumes it. In Live, trace definition → instance value → consuming child property. In Operate Configure, trace form control → VBA handler → changed graphic objects. The worked example supplies the objects; this section explains how their options affect their children.

DeltaV Live · Graphics Studio
DeltaV Operate · Configure / Run

References: [2] [3] [19]
Presence is not runtime Visibility.

Presence determines whether an option appears in the configuration pane. A child’s Visibility/Visible property determines whether its graphic is shown. Keep the option schema and the graphic result separate.

04 / DATA-TO-VISUAL EVALUATION

How does data become a displayed result?

The evaluation flow traces a value through its expression, animation or function into a graphic property. Example: a pump-status value is converted to a color, and that color is used by the pump symbol’s fill. Use it to locate the data source, the conversion rule, the consumer and any fallback when data cannot be resolved.

A function returns a value; the property consumes it. This does not require an operator click. A runtime event sequence instead follows a trigger and the actions it causes. The exposed option may supply an input to either path.

05 / SEQUENCE DIAGRAMS

What happens after a click?

The object owns the trigger; the handler requests another UI; the popup receives context and uses it to resolve data. That call chain is not the same thing as graphic containment.

DeltaV Live · Graphics Studio
DeltaV Operate · Configure / Run

Live popup identity

OpenFaceplateAsync(tag) uses the tag’s configured faceplate association. OpenContextDisplayAsync(name, tag, ...) names a contextual display explicitly. A display-reference property cannot reference contextual displays.

Operate popup identity

A .grf faceplate/detail/custom popup is a graphic document. A UserForm is VBA UI. The same header button could call either; identify the actual target and context-transfer code before comparing behavior.

References: [2] [8] [9] [25]

The Live API topics contain inconsistent legacy examples with placeholder text. The sequence uses the documented Async signatures and argument descriptions, not those ambiguous examples.

06 / ASSOCIATION MODEL

Which hierarchy controls the screen?

There are three independent structures: the object tree inside a graphic, the layout’s screen-space tree, and the display set’s navigation hierarchy. Do not merge them into one tree.

Operate comparison: separate the responsibilities

ResponsibilityLiveOperate Configure / Run
Object containmentDisplay → groups/GEMs/elementsPicture → groups/dynamos/objects
Reusable visual definitionGEM class with linked instances, or unlinked copiesSource dynamo and placed object; inspect update machinery separately
Screen arrangementLayout → screens → display framesConfigured layout/window/header/toolbar assets and opening behavior
Navigation hierarchyDisplay set memberships and levelsNavigation configured by pictures, buttons, helpers and site conventions; no universal equivalent asserted here
Module-specific popupContextual display definition + supplied contextFaceplate/detail picture with context mechanism, or separately a custom UserForm
Authoring toolsExplorer / Palette / Selection / Graphics Configuration / DesignerConfigure workspace / toolbox / dialogs / Experts / VBA editor and custom forms

This comparison identifies responsibilities without inventing a native Operate class hierarchy or claiming that every custom layout follows one implementation.

07 / COMPLETE CLASS VIEW

Class structure, attributes & operations

One coordinated conceptual model of the major graphics responsibilities from Sections 1–6. Switch platforms without moving the canvas. Equal positions and colors mean comparable responsibilities, not automatic conversion or identical implementation.

Model notation, not an SDK declaration. Every member below is an explanatory name. Types such as Context, Geometry and ValueType are model vocabulary. Operations describe what an item or its editor/runtime does; they are not necessarily methods on that item. + marks a public member in this conceptual model, not DeltaV access rights. No undocumented private/protected members are invented.
Read the full class notation: attributes, operations, visibility & relationships
NotationHow to read it
Three compartmentsClass name; typed attributes (state); operations with parameters and return types (behavior).
+ name : StringPublic attribute named name, typed as String. Generic format: visibility name : Type [multiplicity] = default {constraints}.
+ resolve(in context : Context) : AnyPublic operation, input parameter context, return value Any. A missing return type here means it is omitted from this conceptual sketch.
+ / - / # / ~Public / private / protected / package visibility. These are UML member visibility symbols, not operator security levels.
Underlined / italicUnderlined class member: static (classifier scope). Italic class or operation: abstract. Underlined objectName : ClassName instead identifies an object, as in Section 2.
/area : Real {readOnly}Slash marks a derived property. Braces state constraints/modifiers. Multiplicity [0..*] means a collection with zero or more values.
in / out / inoutParameter direction relative to the caller. Default input direction can be omitted. Do not confuse out with the operation return value.
Filled diamond / hollow triangleComposition points from whole to owned part; generalization points from specific type to general type. Composition is not inheritance.
Open arrow / dashed arrowNavigable association / dependency. End multiplicities constrain links, not execution order. Shared aggregation uses a hollow diamond; its precise meaning must be defined by the model.
«interface» and realizationAn implementing class points to its interface with a dashed line and hollow triangle. Neither a native interface hierarchy nor a formal DeltaV stereotype profile is claimed here; guillemet labels describe roles.

live · Documented concepts / model names

ConfigurationLibrary

Repository for reusable definitions. Library Explorer is the authoring view, not a second runtime owner.

What can be created or contained?

Create GEM classes, templates, standards, functions and organizational folders. Languages/themes are also managed in Library Explorer, separately from the four library-item families.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Library organization

Library Explorer organizes GEM classes, templates, Standards and Functions. It is not one graphic with universal Basics/Interaction/Variables tabs. Select a contained definition to configure its own editor.

References: [157]

Limits & distinctions

Definitions are referenced or used as creation sources; placing a graphic does not duplicate this whole repository.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ items : LibraryItem [0..*]

Reusable library definitions: GEM classes, templates, standards and library functions. These are definitions, not placed screen objects.

+ folders : Folder [0..*]

Organization in the Explorer tree. A folder is not another value type or a graphic instance.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ organize(item : LibraryItem)

Organize library definitions into folders through the authoring UI.

+ find(name : String) : LibraryItem

Locate a named reusable definition. This describes the lookup responsibility; it is not a callable find API.

GraphicDocument

A conceptual common category for saved graphical documents, not a concrete item named GraphicDocument in the UI.

What can be created or contained?

Create a Display or Contextual Display. Add supported elements, groups and GEM instances to the chosen document; variables and interactions are configured on the owner.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Conceptual category

GraphicDocument is the model’s shared category. Instantiate Display or Contextual Display, then inspect that concrete document’s actual tabs below through the related-class links.

Limits & distinctions

Do not instantiate the abstract category itself. The active Palette determines what is available.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ elements : GraphicElement [0..*]

Graphic content owned by this document. Groups and GEMs can introduce additional levels of containment.

+ variables : Variable [0..*]

Scoped values or references available to expressions and scripts. A variable is not itself a visible graphic.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ save()

Persist authoring changes. Saving and publishing/deploying are separate actions.

+ publish()

Deploy publishable configuration changes to Live. This is an editor/deployment responsibility, not a method on an SDK class.

+ open(context : Context)

Open the configured document at runtime, optionally with context. Real API selection and arguments are covered in Section 5.

ContextualDisplay

A context-dependent popup definition reused with different tags/modules.

What can be created or contained?

Can contain supported graphics, GEM instances, variables and actions. Faceplates, details and Batch controls are documented examples of contextual displays.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select the popup itself

Select the contextual display root in Selection, or clear the child-element selection on its canvas. Graphics Configuration should identify a contextual display. Basics includes window title and context properties; Interaction additionally includes minimize/restore events.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (5 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles on elements are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Window Title

Enter an expression or reference that resolves to the desired window title when running as a pop–up display window. The default path is Dsp.Tag, which references the tag from the calling display.

Contextual Display Type

Select the type for this contextual display (Faceplate, Detail, FaceplateFB, DetailFB). The contextual display type determines the category that the contextual display uses when performing pinning and replacement functionality. Contextual displays with no type ("--") selected behave as if contextual display pinning is disabled. (For more information on contextual display pinning and replacement functionality, see Customizing DeltaV Live settings specific to a layout in Books Online.)

Allow Debugging

Select this check box to allow the operator to debug errors.

Context Properties (4 fields)

The context properties determine in what context the contextual display is opened. They should be referenced by graphics expressions configured in graphic elements within the contextual display.

Tag Description

The tag description is used online to distinguish and manage a contextual display that has multiple running instances. Enter the primary context–setting value to be used by the contextual display. If you are using this contextual display as a faceplate or detail display for a DeltaV module, node, or device, enter the name of that module, node, or device.

Optional Contexts

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Optional Contexts → Context 1...4 Default Value

Enter the default value for this context.

Optional Contexts → Context 1...4 Description

Enter a description explaining the intended use for this context property (optional).

Size (4 fields)
Width

If you want to customize the size of this contextual display, then select a width and height; do not select an option for the Fit to Display Frame property. Select the width for this contextual display.

Height

If you want to customize the size of this contextual display, then select a width and height; do not select an option for the Fit to Display Frame property. Select the height for this contextual display.

Fit to Display Frame

If you want the size of this contextual display to match an existing display frame, then click the arrow and select the desired display frame. (The layout configuration still determines where this display opens.)

Lock Aspect Ratio

Select the check box to keep the width and height of the display size proportional.

Background (1 fields)
Color

The supplied help contains only a placeholder or incomplete description for this field (Placeholder for background color). Its precise behavior is not established here; check the installed editor/help rather than inferring it from the name.

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

Interaction

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Events (6 fields)
OnOpen

. . . when a contextual display is opened.

OnClose

. . . when a contextual display is closed.

OnActivated

. . . when the pop-up window or display frame in which the contextual display is running becomes activated.

OnDeactivated

. . . when the pop-up window or display frame in which the contextual display is running becomes deactivated.

OnMinimize

. . . when the contextual display is minimized.

OnRestore

. . . when the contextual display is restored to view after being minimized.

Timers (7 fields)
Add Timer

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Timer → Name

Add Timer → Title

Enter a title for the timer. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Add Timer → Description

Enter a description for the timer.

Add Timer → Script

Enter a custom script for the timer. (Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant.) For example, you can write a script that executes only once or a script that runs until a specified condition is met. See the Script Assistant for help on writing a custom script.

Add Timer → Active

Select True to enable this action for this timer. Select False to disable this action for this timer. When False is selected, actions of the same type, on any elements stacked behind this one, are not masked.

Add Timer → Duration

Select the duration (in milliseconds) of the interval between consecutive timer executions.

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Limits & distinctions

The opening action passes context; opening the popup does not make it a child graphic of the clicked button.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ context : Context

The tag/module and any additional context used when opening this UI. Context selects data; it does not copy the popup definition.

+ kind : Faceplate | Detail | Custom

The role or configuration family of the item, rather than an asserted native subclass enumeration.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ initialize(context : Context)

Apply the incoming context and establish the UI’s initial state. Actual initialization events and code vary.

+ activate()

Bring an open UI into its active state; distinguish activation from initial creation/opening.

+ close()

Close the runtime document/UI. Closing does not delete its saved definition.

Follow the connections

Timers (7 fields)

Timers provide a means for users to configure recurring time-delayed actions inside a graphics configuration. When the configuration is open in DeltaV Live, the timer executes its script once at the end of its duration period, as long as its Active property is set to True. If Active is set to False, the timer stops. Then, when Active is set back to True, the script does not execute until a full duration period has passed.

Add Timer

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Timer → Name

Enter a name for the timer.

Add Timer → Title

Enter a title for the timer. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Add Timer → Description

Enter a description for the timer.

Add Timer → Script

Enter a custom script for the timer. (Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant.) For example, you can write a script that executes only once or a script that runs until a specified condition is met. See the Script Assistant for help on writing a custom script.

Add Timer → Active

Select True to enable this action for this timer. Select False to disable this action for this timer. When False is selected, actions of the same type, on any elements stacked behind this one, are not masked.

Add Timer → Duration

Select the duration (in milliseconds) of the interval between consecutive timer executions.

Double-Click triggers a behavior when you double-click on the interaction region. Secondary-Click triggers a behavior when you right-click on the interaction region. Hover triggers a behavior when you hover on the interaction region. Drag allows the user to drag and drop an element into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display.

Choose the scale in which to print the graphic. Don't Scale prints the graphic at 100 percent of its actual size. Pages that do not fit on the selected paper size are cropped and printed on multiple pages. Scale Down reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit. Scale To Fit reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit.

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

If you want additional information to appear when the watch area's OnListUpdated event fires, enter a script calling that information.

Enter the string to appear in front of the rendered value string when the data status is abnormal.

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Interaction Area Border

Select the width for the interaction region.

On properties that have a diamond next to their property field, click the diamond to open a context menu from which you can customize the property (such as apply animations or reference library items). Refer to the topic, Diamond context menu reference , for details on configuring these options.

Variables

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Variables (8 fields)
Add Variable

Click the drop-down arrow and select the type of variable you want to add. The variable is added to the Name/Type/Value table.

Name/Type/Value table

Select a variable in the table to configure its properties. You can configure the following properties for each variable:

Name/Type/Value table → Name

In the Name field, double-click the variable name to enter a new name for the variable. Names must be unique among the elements, GEM Configuration properties, and other variables contained by the group or GEM.

Name/Type/Value table → < Variable > Properties

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

< Variable > Properties → Title

Enter a title for the variable. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

< Variable > Properties → Description

Enter a description for the variable.

< Variable > Properties → Value

Enter or select a value for the variable. The value can be one of the following: Literal value Reference to a standard of a compatible type Simple or library animation Graphics expression

< Variable > Properties → OnWrite

Write a script for the behavior that is triggered when the value of this variable is updated online. Before that value is written to the variable, the OnWrite function verifies that the variable's new value is valid. (For more information on using OnWrite(), refer to the topic, OnWrite function , in the Miscellaneous function section.)

Diamond context menu (29 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. You can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM class Designer.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

References: [35]

Limits & distinctions

An instance of another GEM inside this class is composition/reuse, not inheritance. The Designer exposes options, not a VBA UserForm.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ children : GraphicElement [0..*]

The contained element tree of the reusable source definition. Nested reusable objects are instances in this tree.

+ options : OptionDefinition [0..*]

The custom property schema exposed to a person configuring a GEM instance. See OptionDefinition for the 19 documented property types.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ defineStructure()

Edit the GEM class’s contained graphical elements and nested reusable instances.

+ defineInteractions()

Configure the class’s event behaviors. Linked-instance interactions are edited on the class.

+ saveDefinition()

Save the GEM class definition. A class itself is not published; containing displays are deployed through their publication lifecycle.

Follow the connections

Related guide section → · Back to class canvas

live · Documented concepts / model names

GraphicElement

Abstract category for a placed graphical object. Individual kinds have different properties and legal owners.

What can be created or contained?

Examples in the supplied help include shapes, text, images, data links, buttons, radio buttons, tables, tabs and alarm/Batch controls; groups and GEM instances provide composition. Text can own data placeholders; tabs own tab items.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Choose a concrete element

GraphicElement is a modeling category, not one universal editor. Choose the actual Palette element below to see its documented tabs. This catalog describes controls; it does not imply every control is placeable in every document or GEM.

Open faceplate, detail, or primary control display

Allows the user to acknowledge all alarms in a module or device. Available only for alarm lists showing active alarms.

Allows the user to acknowledge all visible alarms. Available only for alarm lists showing active alarms.

Launch Hardware Alarm Condition Summary

Allows the user to open the Condition Summary application.

Open Alarm Help

Allows the user to open Alarm Help.

Open Alarm Mosaic

Allows the user to open Alarm Mosaic. Available only for alarm lists showing active alarms.

Columns

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Properties (10 fields)
Show Columns in this order

Select the check box next to the column labels you want to appear on this alarm list. The available columns depend on which type of alarm content (active or suppressed) you selected in the Basics tab. In DeltaV Live, the selected columns are shown in the order they appear in this list. In the following tables, the term 'container' refers to either a module or a device. Alarm list columns for active alarms Label Description Ack The state of the alarm represented by one of the following symbols: State Symbol Active-Unacked Blank Active-Acked Inactive-Unacked Inactive-LocalAck Time In Time that the alarm occurred. This column is formatted on the Alarm List element's Basics tab, in the Time section. Unit The name of the unit associated with this alarm's container. This column is blank if the alarm is not associated with a unit. Module/Param An Alarm ID consisting of the container module name and alarm parameter name. Description The description string configured for the alarm's container. Alarm For process alarms: The alarm word configured for the alarm type (for example, HIHI) For device alarms: The alarm word derived from the alarm parameter (for example, FAILED) Message The alarm message string. Priority The alarm priority word configured for the alarm's current priority (for example, CRITICAL). Area The name of the area associated with the alarm's container. Category For process alarms: The category word configured for the alarm type For device alarms: The localized string for the word DEVICE Classification The functional classification specified for the alarm. Help An icon or blank indicating the availability of Alarm Help for this alarm. Module The name of the alarm's container module. Node The name of the DeltaV node where the alarm originated (for example, CTLR_1). Param The alarm parameter name. Part of A string displaying the name of the top level module containing this module. That is, the path including the topmost module where the alarm is occurring. Time Last Time of the last state change. This column is formatted on the Alarm List element's Basics tab, in the Time section. Zone The DeltaV zone where the alarm originated. Value The process value (or current value) for the alarm. Shows the numeric value only, without engineering units. Limit The value at which the alarm condition is true. Shows the limit only, without engineering units. Units The engineering units defined for the value. Value/Units The alarm's process value (or current value) with engineering units. Limit/Units The alarm's limit with engineering units. Alarm list columns for suppressed alarms Label Description Time In Time that the alarm occurred. This column is formatted on the Alarm List element's Basics tab, in the Time section. Unit The name of the unit associated with this alarm's container. This column is blank if the alarm is not associated with a unit. Module/Param An Alarm ID consisting of the container module name and alarm parameter name. Description The description string configured for the alarm's container. Alarm For process alarms: The alarm word configured for the alarm type (for example, HIHI) For device alarms: The alarm word derived from the alarm parameter (for example, FAILED) Priority The alarm priority word configured for the alarm's current priority (for example, CRITICAL). Area The name of the area associated with the alarm's container. Category For process alarms: The category word configured for the alarm type For device alarms: The localized string for the word DEVICE Classification The functional classification specified for the alarm. Help An icon or blank indicating the availability of Alarm Help for this alarm. Module The name of the alarm's container module. Node The name of the DeltaV node where the alarm originated (for example, CTLR_1). Param The alarm parameter name. Part of A string displaying the name of the top level module containing this module. That is, the path including the topmost module where the alarm is occurring. Zone The DeltaV zone where the alarm originated. Shelved Timer The remaining shelving time for the alarm. If an alarm is out of service, this column is blank. Suppression Reason The suppression reason specified for the alarm. Configure the following three properties for each column you select.

Show Columns in this order → Initial Width

Select the initial column width for the selected column.

Show Columns in this order → Coloring By

Select the alarm color scheme for the selected column (by Background , Alarm Category , or Alarm Priority ).

Show Columns in this order → Click Action

Select the associated click action for the selected column.

Show Column Headers

Select this check box to show column headers for all columns selected above.

Show Column Headers → Font

Select the font, font size, and font style for the column headers.

Show Column Headers → Text Color

Select the text color for the column headers.

Show Column Headers → Background

Select the background color for the column headers.

Single Click-Actions Enabled

Select True to allow all associated actions (as set with the Click Action property) to trigger on a single click of the left mouse button. Select False to require operators to select a field and then click again to trigger the associated action.

Allow Column Resizing

Select this check box to show alarms filtered by areas, modules, or devices. When selected, also configure the following properties:

Filter by Plant Hierarchy → Context

Select Current to use the name of the current context as the source for alarms. Select Specific to use user-specified contexts as the sources for alarms.

Context → Treat Current Name as

Select whether to treat the current name as an Area , UM/EM (unit module/equipment module), or Module/Device .

Context → Current Name

Enter the path or an expression that resolves to the name for the current context.

Context → Names are for

Enter the names of up to five sources (plant area, unit, module, or device) to use as the contexts for the alarms. Select whether the specified names are for an Area , UM/EM (unit module/equipment module), or Module/Device .

Filter by Alarm Priorities

Select this check box to show alarms by their alarm priority.

Filter by Alarm Priorities → Priority

Select Same as Alarm Banner to use the same priorities as set in the Alarm Banner. Select By Alarm Classification to use the same priorities as set for alarm classifications.

Show only recent alarms

Select this check box to show alarms that occurred within the specified time range.

Show only recent alarms → Show only recent alarms

Specify the time range by selecting the number of days, hours, and/or minutes.

Show only with a specific Functional Classification

Select this check box to show only the alarms in a specific functional classification.

Show only with a specific Functional Classification → Function Classification

Select the functional classification from which to show alarms.

Show only with a specific category

Select this check box to show only the alarms in a specific category.

Show only with a specific category → Category

Select the category from which to show alarms.

Show only with suppressed alarms

Select this check box to show only suppressed alarms.

Show only with suppressed alarms → Suppression Type

Select whether to show Shelved alarms or Removed from Service alarms.

Exclude Unacknowledged Inactive Alarms

Select this check box to exclude unacknowledged inactive alarms from the list, regardless of other filters selected.

Sorting (1 fields)
Sorting

Select the sort order for the alarms in the list. Ack/State/Time In - Sorts alarms by acknowledged alarms, alarm state, and time they occurred. Time In - Sorts alarms by the time they occurred. Time Last - Sorts alarms by the time of their last state change. Alarm Id - Sorts alarms by their module name and alarm name. Priority/Suppression Timer - Sorts alarms by their remaining suppression time. This option is available only when Suppressed is selected as the Alarm Content (in the Basics tab / Alarm List section).

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Interaction (71 fields)

Click Add Action to create and configure one of the following actions on this element: Click Action triggers a behavior when you click once on the interaction region. Double-Click triggers a behavior when you double-click on the interaction region. Secondary-Click triggers a behavior when you right-click on the interaction region. Hover triggers a behavior when you hover on the interaction region. Drag allows the user to drag and drop an element into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → No behavior

No Behavior either triggers no actions of this type on this element or masks the same type of action on an element stacked behind it (provided that the Active property is True ).

No behavior → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Custom Script

When the action is triggered, this behavior runs a custom script.

Custom Script → Script

Enter the script to be run, or click Edit Script to use the Script Assistant.

Custom Script → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Write Value to Destination

When the action is triggered, this behavior shows a specified value in a specified location.

Write Value to Destination → Value

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the desired value.

Write Value to Destination → Destination

If the Write Destination is a DeltaV parameter, enter the parameter reference that resolves to that parameter. Example 1: DLSYS["FIC101/PID1/MODE.TARGET"] Example 2: DLSYS[Grp.ModuleName + "/PID1/SP"]

Write Value to Destination → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → SIS Write Value to Destination

When the action is triggered, this behavior shows a specified value in a specified location.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Value

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the desired value.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Parameter Path

Enter the parameter reference that resolves to the desired parameter. Example 1: DLSYS["FIC101/PID1/MODE.TARGET"] Example 2: DLSYS[Grp.ModuleName + "/PID1/SP"]

SIS Write Value to Destination → Confirmation Information

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the confirmation message string presented in the confirmation dialog(s) at the time of the write attempt.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Primary Control Display

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the primary control display for the specified module.

Open Primary Control Display → Module

Enter the expression that resolves to the module associated with the primary control display to be opened.

Open Primary Control Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Display

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified display.

Open Display → Display

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the name of the display to be opened.

Open Display → Placement Option

Select In Layout to specify the display frame in which a display should open. Select Standard to apply the standard rules for opening a display according to its display level. Select Popup to open a display as a pop-up window.

Placement Option → Target Display Frames

If you have selected In Layout as the placement option, enter the name of the display frame in which the display opens. Tip : You can also specify multiple target display frames in which the display should open. This option is helpful when a display needs to be opened in various layouts. (Use commas to separate display frame names.) When more than one display frame is specified, the display opens in the first display frame specified that exists in the current layout. If the current layout does not contain any display frames matching the names provided in this field, then the display does not open.

Open Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Print

When the trigger action occurs, this behavior prints the graphic(s) specified in the Scope property.

Print → Show Print Dialog

Select True to open the Print dialog when this action is triggered. If True, the operator can use the Print dialog to change print settings configured on this action.

Print → Scope

Select the graphic(s) to be printed when this action is triggered. All Screens prints all screens in the layout, with each screen on its own page. Specific Screen prints the screen specified in Screen Name . This Screen prints the screen containing the display on which this action is configured. This Display prints the display on which this action is configured.

Print → Screen Name

This property is available only when Specific Screen is selected for the Scope property. Enter or browse to the name of the screen to be printed.

Print → Scale

Choose the scale in which to print the graphic. Don't Scale prints the graphic at 100 percent of its actual size. Pages that do not fit on the selected paper size are cropped and printed on multiple pages. Scale Down reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit. Scale To Fit reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit.

Print → Orientation

Choose the orientation mode for your graphics. Portrait prints the graphic vertically. Landscape prints the graphic horizontally. Best Fit prints the graphic in the orientation that best fits it.

Print → Printer Name

Select the printer.

Print → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Contextual Display

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified contextual display.

Open Contextual Display → Contextual Display

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the name of the contextual display to be opened.

Open Contextual Display → Tag

Enter the tag for the module, node, or device name that is to be used for the primary context value. (The tag must be in quotes. For example, "FIC-102 " .

Open Contextual Display → Optional Contexts

Select the check box next to each context (Context 1... N ) you want to configure. For each context property selected, enter an expression that resolves to the module, node, or device name to be used for this context value.

Open Contextual Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Faceplate

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the faceplate associated with the specified tag.

Open Faceplate → Tag

Enter the tag for the module, node, or device name that is to be used for the primary context value. (The tag must be in quotes. For example, "FIC-102 " .

Open Faceplate → Optional Contexts

Select the check box next to each context (Context 1... N ) you want to configure. For each context property selected, enter an expression that resolves to the module, node, or device name to be used for this context value.

Open Faceplate → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Detail

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the detail display associated with the specified tag.

Open Detail → Tag

Enter the tag for the module, node, or device name that is to be used for the primary context value. (The tag must be in quotes. For example, "FIC-102 " .

Open Detail → Optional Contexts

Select the check box next to each context (Context 1... N ) you want to configure. For each context property selected, enter an expression that resolves to the module, node, or device name to be used for this context value.

Open Detail → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Application

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified application.

Open Application → DeltaV Application

Select True if you want the action to open a DeltaV application included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list. Select False if you want the action to open an application that is not included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list.

Open Application → DeltaV Application Name

This property is available only when you have selected True for DeltaV Application . Click the drop-down arrow and select the name of the application to be opened.

Open Application → Application Path

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property references a Private String library standard and populates the path to the application you want to open. Do one of the following for this property: From the drop-down list, select the Private String standard that corresponds to the application to be opened. (All existing Private String standards are included as options in this list.) Using the Diamond context menu, create a new Private String standard for the application to be opened and then select that standard from the drop-down list. Note : When creating a private string standard, note the following: If the application to be opened is not digitally signed, the private string must have the command argument, NoSignatureCheck , appended to the end of the directory path. Example 1 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open Notepad, enter C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe;NoSignatureCheck as the value. Example 2 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open the InfoLog, enter C:\Program Files (x86)\Internet Explorer\iexplore.exe; NoSignatureCheck as the value.

Open Application → Command Arguments

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property resolves to a string that will be used as the command line argument(s) supplied when the application is launched. Continuing Example 2 from the Application Path property, after creating a private string standard to open InfoLog, enter -k\https://logbooksserver\ as the command argument.

Open Application → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Content as Tooltip → Dynamic Value

Enter an expression that determines the value to appear in the tooltip.

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Drag

A drag action configured on an element allows the user to drag and drop the element's process value into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display. For this action, configure the following properties:

Add Action: Drag → History Server Preference

Enter the preferred historical data source.

Add Action: Drag → Parameter

Enter the parameter you want available as a watch list item. When a user drags the element on which this action is configured into a watch area or a Process History View chart, this parameter appears as a watch list item. (If a title is configured, the title appears in place of the parameter path.)

Add Action: Drag → Title

(Optional) Enter the friendly name to appear on the watch list item. (If no title is configured, the parameter path appears in place of the title.)

Add Action: Drag → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Add Action: Drag → Content

If you want additional information to appear when the watch area's OnListUpdated event fires, enter a script calling that information.

Add Action: Drag → Abnormal Status Prefix

Enter the string to appear in front of the rendered value string when the data status is abnormal.

Add Action: Drag → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Interaction Area (1 fields)
Interaction Area Border

Select the width for the interaction region.

Diamond Context Menu (0 fields)

On properties that have a diamond next to their property field, click the diamond to open a context menu from which you can customize the property (such as apply animations or reference library items). Refer to the topic, Diamond context menu reference , for details on configuring these options.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles on elements are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Circle Segment (2 fields)
Start Angle

Select the desired distance from the element's end point to its start angle.

End Angle

Select the desired distance from the element's end point to its end angle.

Fill (4 fields)
Fill Color

Select the fill color for the element.

Fill Percent

Select the percentage of the element the fill color occupies.

Fill Angle

Select the angle for the fill color. The direction of the fill angle corresponds to the element's orientation. In other words, if the element rotates, the fill angle rotates with it. The fill angle is visible only when Fill Percent is less than 100 percent.

Background

Select the background color (the color behind the element's fill color) for the element. The background color is visible only when Fill Percent is greater or less than 100 percent.

Line (7 fields)
Line Color

Select the border color for the element.

Line Thickness

Select the border thickness for the element.

Line Style

Select the border style for the element.

Arrow Start Type

Select the shape of the arrow at the start of the line.

Arrow Start Size

Select the size of the arrow at the start of the line.

Arrow End Type

Select the shape of the arrow at the end of the line.

Arrow End Size

Select the size of the arrow at the end of the line.

Geometry (5 fields)
Width

Select the width for the element.

Height

Select the height for the element.

Rotation Angle

Select the measure of degrees the element rotates about a fixed point.

Horizontal Position

Select the horizontal distance from the left side of the display to the element's center point (point of rotation).

Vertical Position

Select the vertical distance from the top of the display to the element's center point (point of rotation).

Visibility (3 fields)
Visibility

Select Visible to keep the element visible and enable its configured online actions, if any. Select Hidden to hide the element and disable any configured online actions.

Blink

Select True to have the element blink on and off, according to the selected Blink Style . Select False to prevent the element from blinking.

Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.
