Button · Interaction

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Events (6 fields)
OnTab

After completing a data entry, moves input focus to the next data entry element.

OnBackTab

After completing a data entry, moves input focus to the next data entry element, in the reverse direction of OnTab.

OnEnter

When the user completes the entry, this event checks and corrects the entry. For combo boxes, check boxes and radio buttons: An entry is considered complete when the user chooses or switches to a new value. For text entry elements: An entry is considered complete when the user presses Enter.

OnTab

Moves input focus to another data entry element after a data entry is completed.

OnBackTab

Moves input focus to another data entry element, in the reverse direction of OnTab, after a data entry is completed.

OnEnter

Checks and corrects the entry when the user indicates the entry is completed. For combo boxes, check boxes and radio buttons, an entry is considered complete when the user chooses or switches to a new value. For text entry elements, an entry is considered complete when the user presses Enter.

Button (0 fields)

Use this section to configure the action that occurs when the user clicks this button. If you configure the click action here, it is propagated to the other two configuration places. For detailed help on configuring the specific behavior for the click action, refer to the behavior descriptions in this topic's Interaction section.

Interaction (71 fields)

Click Add Action to create and configure one of the following actions on this element: Click Action triggers a behavior when you click once on the interaction region. Double-Click triggers a behavior when you double-click on the interaction region. Secondary-Click triggers a behavior when you right-click on the interaction region. Hover triggers a behavior when you hover on the interaction region. Drag allows the user to drag and drop an element into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → No behavior

No Behavior either triggers no actions of this type on this element or masks the same type of action on an element stacked behind it (provided that the Active property is True ).

No behavior → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Custom Script

When the action is triggered, this behavior runs a custom script.

Custom Script → Script

Enter the script to be run, or click Edit Script to use the Script Assistant.

Custom Script → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Write Value to Destination

When the action is triggered, this behavior shows a specified value in a specified location.

Write Value to Destination → Value

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the desired value.

Write Value to Destination → Destination

If the Write Destination is a DeltaV parameter, enter the parameter reference that resolves to that parameter. Example 1: DLSYS["FIC101/PID1/MODE.TARGET"] Example 2: DLSYS[Grp.ModuleName + "/PID1/SP"]

Write Value to Destination → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → SIS Write Value to Destination

When the action is triggered, this behavior shows a specified value in a specified location.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Value

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the desired value.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Parameter Path

Enter the parameter reference that resolves to the desired parameter. Example 1: DLSYS["FIC101/PID1/MODE.TARGET"] Example 2: DLSYS[Grp.ModuleName + "/PID1/SP"]

SIS Write Value to Destination → Confirmation Information

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the confirmation message string presented in the confirmation dialog(s) at the time of the write attempt.

SIS Write Value to Destination → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the primary control display for the specified module.

Open Primary Control Display → Module

Enter the expression that resolves to the module associated with the primary control display to be opened.

Open Primary Control Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Display

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified display.

Open Display → Display

Enter a graphics expression that resolves to the name of the display to be opened.

Open Display → Placement Option

Select In Layout to specify the display frame in which a display should open. Select Standard to apply the standard rules for opening a display according to its display level. Select Popup to open a display as a pop-up window.

Placement Option → Target Display Frames

If you have selected In Layout as the placement option, enter the name of the display frame in which the display opens. Tip : You can also specify multiple target display frames in which the display should open. This option is helpful when a display needs to be opened in various layouts. (Use commas to separate display frame names.) When more than one display frame is specified, the display opens in the first display frame specified that exists in the current layout. If the current layout does not contain any display frames matching the names provided in this field, then the display does not open.

Open Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Print

When the trigger action occurs, this behavior prints the graphic(s) specified in the Scope property.

Print → Show Print Dialog

Select True to open the Print dialog when this action is triggered. If True, the operator can use the Print dialog to change print settings configured on this action.

Print → Scope

Select the graphic(s) to be printed when this action is triggered. All Screens prints all screens in the layout, with each screen on its own page. Specific Screen prints the screen specified in Screen Name . This Screen prints the screen containing the display on which this action is configured. This Display prints the display on which this action is configured.

Print → Screen Name

This property is available only when Specific Screen is selected for the Scope property. Enter or browse to the name of the screen to be printed.

Print → Scale

Choose the scale in which to print the graphic. Don't Scale prints the graphic at 100 percent of its actual size. Pages that do not fit on the selected paper size are cropped and printed on multiple pages. Scale Down reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit. Scale To Fit reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit.

Print → Orientation

Choose the orientation mode for your graphics. Portrait prints the graphic vertically. Landscape prints the graphic horizontally. Best Fit prints the graphic in the orientation that best fits it.

Print → Printer Name

Select the printer.

Print → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Enter the tag for the module, node, or device name that is to be used for the primary context value. (The tag must be in quotes. For example, "FIC-102 " .

Open Contextual Display → Optional Contexts

Select the check box next to each context (Context 1... N ) you want to configure. For each context property selected, enter an expression that resolves to the module, node, or device name to be used for this context value.

Open Contextual Display → Active

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Select whether this action is enabled (True) or disabled (False) on this element in runtime. When you select False , the following applies: On any elements stacked behind this one, actions of the same type are not masked. Both the behavior and the hotspot are disabled on the selected element.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Open Application

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified application.

Open Application → DeltaV Application

Select True if you want the action to open a DeltaV application included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list. Select False if you want the action to open an application that is not included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list.

Open Application → DeltaV Application Name

This property is available only when you have selected True for DeltaV Application . Click the drop-down arrow and select the name of the application to be opened.

Open Application → Application Path

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property references a Private String library standard and populates the path to the application you want to open. Do one of the following for this property: From the drop-down list, select the Private String standard that corresponds to the application to be opened. (All existing Private String standards are included as options in this list.) Using the Diamond context menu, create a new Private String standard for the application to be opened and then select that standard from the drop-down list. Note : When creating a private string standard, note the following: If the application to be opened is not digitally signed, the private string must have the command argument, NoSignatureCheck , appended to the end of the directory path. Example 1 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open Notepad, enter C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe;NoSignatureCheck as the value. Example 2 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open the InfoLog, enter C:\Program Files (x86)\Internet Explorer\iexplore.exe; NoSignatureCheck as the value.

Open Application → Command Arguments

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property resolves to a string that will be used as the command line argument(s) supplied when the application is launched. Continuing Example 2 from the Application Path property, after creating a private string standard to open InfoLog, enter -k\https://logbooksserver\ as the command argument.

Limits & distinctions

Trigger availability varies. A timer belongs to configuration, not to a library function just because both execute code.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ trigger : EventKind

The configured occurrence that invokes a behavior, such as click or hover. Available triggers depend on the owning element.

+ action : ActionDefinition

The selected behavior and its configuration: for example, a popup request, a write action or a custom script.

+ owner : EventOwner

The document, layout or graphic element that owns this behavior. EventOwner is conceptual shorthand, not an internal runtime object type. Its supported triggers depend on that owner.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ handle(event : Event)

Execute the behavior/procedure associated with an event. Actual trigger and handler signatures depend on the owner.

+ resolveContext() : Context

Determine the tag/module and additional values to pass to the requested UI.

+ requestPopup(context : Context)

Ask runtime to open the configured popup with context. In Operate the target may be a picture or a separate UserForm.

live · Documented concepts / model names

GEMInstance

A placed GEM, either linked to a class or unlinked.

What can be created or contained?

Linked: instance options and eligible overrides. Unlinked: add an existing GEM instance, group or single display element; customize its own property schema. Nested links can remain.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Linked versus unlinked

Basics applies to both. Linked GEMs expose Variables and conditional Overrides; their class owns shared interactions. Unlinked GEMs have their own Interaction and Variables topics. Basic Configuration fields vary by GEM; the installed-GEM examples below are not mandatory fields on every custom GEM.

This option appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On unlinked GEMs only: To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's GEM Configuration Designer and Basics tab. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. You can modify the value of the new property on the Basics tab.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

GEM (linked) · Overrides

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Override columns (3 fields)

Visible only when overrides exist. Includes overrides on nested components.

Element

Expand the element hierarchy to locate the overridden property.

Override

The current instance override value. You can modify it here.

Class

The corresponding class value; the instance uses its override while the override remains.

Properties (3 fields)
Element

A hierarchical list of the elements containing overrides, beginning with the override's outermost element. Click the expander arrows to drill down to the override property.

Override

The property's current value of the override. This value can be modified here.

Class

The property's value in the GEM class. Note that while the override is present, the property uses the override value.

Unbound overrides (0 fields)

Overrides are preserved as long as the component and property containing the override exist in the class by their original names. When an override cannot find a matching component name or property name, it becomes an unbound override. If you want to rebind the override, verify the following: Does the GEM class for this linked GEM exist in the configuration database? Has the component containing the override property been deleted from the GEM class? For more information on unbound overrides, see the related topic on using overrides to modify linked GEMs.

Interaction (71 fields)

Click Add Action to create and configure one of the following actions on this element: Click Action triggers a behavior when you click once on the interaction region. Double-Click triggers a behavior when you double-click on the interaction region. Secondary-Click triggers a behavior when you right-click on the interaction region. Hover triggers a behavior when you hover on the interaction region. Drag allows the user to drag and drop an element into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display.

When the trigger action occurs, this behavior prints the graphic(s) specified in the Scope property.

Print → Show Print Dialog

Select True to open the Print dialog when this action is triggered. If True, the operator can use the Print dialog to change print settings configured on this action.

Print → Scope

Select the graphic(s) to be printed when this action is triggered. All Screens prints all screens in the layout, with each screen on its own page. Specific Screen prints the screen specified in Screen Name . This Screen prints the screen containing the display on which this action is configured. This Display prints the display on which this action is configured.

Print → Screen Name

This property is available only when Specific Screen is selected for the Scope property. Enter or browse to the name of the screen to be printed.

Print → Scale

Choose the scale in which to print the graphic. Don't Scale prints the graphic at 100 percent of its actual size. Pages that do not fit on the selected paper size are cropped and printed on multiple pages. Scale Down reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit. Scale To Fit reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit.

Print → Orientation

Choose the orientation mode for your graphics. Portrait prints the graphic vertically. Landscape prints the graphic horizontally. Best Fit prints the graphic in the orientation that best fits it.

Print → Printer Name

Select the printer.

When the action is triggered, this behavior opens the specified application.

Open Application → DeltaV Application

Select True if you want the action to open a DeltaV application included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list. Select False if you want the action to open an application that is not included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list.

Open Application → DeltaV Application Name

This property is available only when you have selected True for DeltaV Application . Click the drop-down arrow and select the name of the application to be opened.

Open Application → Application Path

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property references a Private String library standard and populates the path to the application you want to open. Do one of the following for this property: From the drop-down list, select the Private String standard that corresponds to the application to be opened. (All existing Private String standards are included as options in this list.) Using the Diamond context menu, create a new Private String standard for the application to be opened and then select that standard from the drop-down list. Note : When creating a private string standard, note the following: If the application to be opened is not digitally signed, the private string must have the command argument, NoSignatureCheck , appended to the end of the directory path. Example 1 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open Notepad, enter C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe;NoSignatureCheck as the value. Example 2 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open the InfoLog, enter C:\Program Files (x86)\Internet Explorer\iexplore.exe; NoSignatureCheck as the value.

Open Application → Command Arguments

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property resolves to a string that will be used as the command line argument(s) supplied when the application is launched. Continuing Example 2 from the Application Path property, after creating a private string standard to open InfoLog, enter -k\https://logbooksserver\ as the command argument.

Timers (7 fields)

Timers provide a means for users to configure recurring time-delayed actions inside a graphics configuration. When the configuration is open in DeltaV Live, the timer executes its script once at the end of its duration period, as long as its Active property is set to True. If Active is set to False, the timer stops. Then, when Active is set back to True, the script does not execute until a full duration period has passed.

Add Timer

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Timer → Name

Enter a name for the timer.

Add Timer → Title

Enter a title for the timer. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Add Timer → Description

Enter a description for the timer.

Add Timer → Script

Enter a custom script for the timer. (Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant.) For example, you can write a script that executes only once or a script that runs until a specified condition is met. See the Script Assistant for help on writing a custom script.

Add Timer → Active

Select True to enable this action for this timer. Select False to disable this action for this timer. When False is selected, actions of the same type, on any elements stacked behind this one, are not masked.

Add Timer → Duration

Select the duration (in milliseconds) of the interval between consecutive timer executions.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

References: [69]

Limits & distinctions

Do not add/remove child structure on a linked instance as if it were an ordinary unlinked container. Edit the class or intentionally unlink.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ classRef : GEMClass [0..1]

The shared GEM class tracked by a linked instance. An unlinked GEM has no outer class reference; nested instances can still be linked.

+ linked : Boolean

Whether this placement tracks a GEM class. Being linked restricts structural edits and changes the rules for overrides.

+ values : OptionValue [0..*]

The instance’s configured values for exposed GEM options. The class defines what options exist; each placement supplies values.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ setOption(name : String, value : Any)

Assign a value to an exposed instance option, using the option’s allowed type and configuration rules.

+ overrideEligibleProperty()

Override an eligible nested property on a linked GEM. This does not allow adding/removing child elements or changing nested animations.

+ unlink()

Remove the outer instance’s GEM-class link. Nested GEM links may remain.

live · Documented concepts / model names

Group

Local composition of one or more graphical elements.

What can be created or contained?

Group members can be graphical elements, including existing groups/GEM content as supported by the editor. Groups can have scoped variables and supported behavior.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select the group

Select the Group itself, not a child. Its Basics, Interaction and Variables configure the local container; nested children retain their own properties.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a title for the group (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter other information describing the group (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Geometry (5 fields)
Width

Select the width for the group. The width proportionately resizes (and repositions) all members of the group to fit in the resized bounding box.

Height

Select the height for the group. The height proportionately resizes (and repositions) all members of the group to fit in the resized bounding box.

Rotation Angle

Select the measure of degrees the group rotates about a fixed point. When Rotation Angle is not animated, the group's center point is automatically determined as the center point of the bounding box encompassing all members of the group.

Horizontal Position

Select the horizontal distance from the left side of the display to the group's center point (point of rotation). A group's Horizontal Position starts from the left-most member of the group.

Vertical Position

Select the vertical distance from the top of the display to the group's center point (point of rotation). A group's Vertical Position starts from the left-most member of the group.

Visibility (4 fields)
Visibility

Select Visible to keep the group visible and to enable its configured online actions, if any. If individual group members are hidden, they stay hidden, even when the group's Visibility is configured as Visible. Select Hidden to hide the group and to disable configured online actions, if any. All group members are hidden, even if their individual Visibility properties are configured as Visible. Note : Changing the Visibility value of a group does not change the configured Visibility value or animation of its members.

Blink

Select True to have the group blink on and off, according to its blink period. Select False to prevent the group from blinking.

Blink Period

Select the length of time, in seconds, between blinks. Note : A group's Blink and Blink Period values take precedence over the Blink and Blink Period values of individual group members. That is, when a group's Blink is True, all of its group members behave as if their Blink property is False, so that they all appear to blink as a group.

Present Online

Select this check box to include all elements in the group or GEM when the graphics configuration is published online. The property provides a means to include a complex element on a contextual display (or display) during configuration, but to configure it to not consume resources when online.

Placement Option → Target Display Frames

If you have selected In Layout as the placement option, enter the name of the display frame in which the display opens. Tip : You can also specify multiple target display frames in which the display should open. This option is helpful when a display needs to be opened in various layouts. (Use commas to separate display frame names.) When more than one display frame is specified, the display opens in the first display frame specified that exists in the current layout. If the current layout does not contain any display frames matching the names provided in this field, then the display does not open.

Add Action: Click Action, Double-click, Secondary-click, and Hover → Print

When the trigger action occurs, this behavior prints the graphic(s) specified in the Scope property.

Print → Show Print Dialog

Select True to open the Print dialog when this action is triggered. If True, the operator can use the Print dialog to change print settings configured on this action.

Print → Scope

Select the graphic(s) to be printed when this action is triggered. All Screens prints all screens in the layout, with each screen on its own page. Specific Screen prints the screen specified in Screen Name . This Screen prints the screen containing the display on which this action is configured. This Display prints the display on which this action is configured.

Print → Screen Name

This property is available only when Specific Screen is selected for the Scope property. Enter or browse to the name of the screen to be printed.

Print → Scale

Choose the scale in which to print the graphic. Don't Scale prints the graphic at 100 percent of its actual size. Pages that do not fit on the selected paper size are cropped and printed on multiple pages. Scale Down reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit. Scale To Fit reduces each page to fit the printable area of the currently selected paper size, with a .2-inch margin. If a page is too large for the printable area, it is automatically scaled to fit.

Print → Orientation

Choose the orientation mode for your graphics. Portrait prints the graphic vertically. Landscape prints the graphic horizontally. Best Fit prints the graphic in the orientation that best fits it.

Print → Printer Name

Select the printer.

Open Application → DeltaV Application

Select True if you want the action to open a DeltaV application included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list. Select False if you want the action to open an application that is not included in the DeltaV Application Name drop-down list.

Open Application → DeltaV Application Name

This property is available only when you have selected True for DeltaV Application . Click the drop-down arrow and select the name of the application to be opened.

Open Application → Application Path

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property references a Private String library standard and populates the path to the application you want to open. Do one of the following for this property: From the drop-down list, select the Private String standard that corresponds to the application to be opened. (All existing Private String standards are included as options in this list.) Using the Diamond context menu, create a new Private String standard for the application to be opened and then select that standard from the drop-down list. Note : When creating a private string standard, note the following: If the application to be opened is not digitally signed, the private string must have the command argument, NoSignatureCheck , appended to the end of the directory path. Example 1 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open Notepad, enter C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe;NoSignatureCheck as the value. Example 2 — To create a private string standard that will be used to open the InfoLog, enter C:\Program Files (x86)\Internet Explorer\iexplore.exe; NoSignatureCheck as the value.

Open Application → Command Arguments

This property is available only when you have selected False for DeltaV Application . This property resolves to a string that will be used as the command line argument(s) supplied when the application is launched. Continuing Example 2 from the Application Path property, after creating a private string standard to open InfoLog, enter -k\https://logbooksserver\ as the command argument.

Add Action: Drag

A drag action configured on an element allows the user to drag and drop the element's process value into a watch area or a Process History View chart on a running display. For this action, configure the following properties:

Timers (7 fields)

Timers provide a means for users to configure recurring time-delayed actions inside a graphics configuration. When the configuration is open in DeltaV Live, the timer executes its script once at the end of its duration period, as long as its Active property is set to True. If Active is set to False, the timer stops. Then, when Active is set back to True, the script does not execute until a full duration period has passed.

Add Timer

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Timer → Name

Enter a name for the timer.

Add Timer → Title

Enter a title for the timer. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Add Timer → Description

Enter a description for the timer.

Add Timer → Script

Enter a custom script for the timer. (Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant.) For example, you can write a script that executes only once or a script that runs until a specified condition is met. See the Script Assistant for help on writing a custom script.

Add Timer → Active

Select True to enable this action for this timer. Select False to disable this action for this timer. When False is selected, actions of the same type, on any elements stacked behind this one, are not masked.

Add Timer → Duration

Select the duration (in milliseconds) of the interval between consecutive timer executions.

Diamond context menu (0 fields)

On properties that have a diamond next to their property field, click the diamond to open a context menu from which you can customize the property (such as apply animations or reference library items). Refer to the topic, Diamond context menu reference , for details on configuring these options.

Variables (8 fields)
Add Variable

Click the drop-down arrow and select the type of variable you want to add. The variable is added to the Name/Type/Value table.

Name/Type/Value

Select a variable in the table to configure its properties. You can configure the following properties for each variable:

Name/Type/Value → Name

In the Name field, double-click the variable name to enter a new name for the variable. Names must be unique among the elements, GEM Configuration properties, and other variables contained by the group or GEM.

Name/Type/Value → Variable Properties

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Variable Properties → Title

Enter a title for the variable. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Variable Properties → Description

Enter a description for the variable.

Variable Properties → Value

Enter or select a value for the variable. The value can be one of the following: Literal value Reference to a standard of a compatible type Simple or library animation Graphics expression

Variable Properties → OnWrite

Write a script for the behavior that is triggered when the value of this variable is updated online. Before that value is written to the variable, the OnWrite function verifies that the variable's new value is valid. (For more details on using the OnWrite function, refer to the topic, OnWrite function , in the Miscellaneous function section.)

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

Limits & distinctions

A Group has no GEM Configuration Designer or GEM class link. Grouping and reusable class creation solve different problems.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ members : GraphicElement [0..*]

The graphic elements grouped together. The group owns this local collection; grouping does not create a shared GEM class.

+ variables : Variable [0..*]

Scoped values or references available to expressions and scripts. A variable is not itself a visible graphic.

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ add(element : GraphicElement)

Add an eligible graphic to the local container using the authoring workflow. This is not unrestricted runtime object creation.

+ remove(element : GraphicElement)

Remove a member from this container in the model. The actual editor command determines whether it is deleted, moved or ungrouped.

+ transform(geometry : Geometry)

Apply position/size/transformation changes to the container and its members according to editor behavior.

Variable types — 8 documented choices

Color

Font

Image

Measurement

Number

Limits & distinctions

A reference to an online parameter, Standard or another reference is read-only online. Variable types are listed below.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ type : ValueType

The allowed value family. See the type catalog below: a Standard type, a variable type and a GEM option type are different catalogs.

+ source : Literal | Reference

Where a value comes from: a literal, a reference or an expression, as indicated in the signature. Reference-backed Live variables can be read-only online.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ read() : Any

Retrieve the variable’s value. A read does not imply a controller write or creation of a graphic.

+ assign(value : Any) {if writable}

Set the value where writable. Live variables backed by online parameters, standards or references cannot be assigned online as ordinary mutable variables.

OptionDefinition

Schema for an exposed custom GEM option. These are the options a user configures on a placement.

What can be created or contained?

Create property groups and the 19 documented property types below in the GEM Configuration Designer. Information, Value and Presence configure the option.

Actual editor / configuration surface

GEM Configuration Designer

OptionDefinition is our name for a custom GEM configuration property. In Design, add a property group and property type, then configure Information, Value and Presence. These are Designer groups, not a universal class tab set.

References: [3]
Information → Title / Description / Tooltip

Explain the purpose of the exposed option to the engineer configuring an instance.

Value → Default value

Set the initial instance option value on the class. This is distinct from changing one placed instance.

Boolean → Presentation

Choose whether the Boolean option is presented as a check box or combo box.

Numeric type → Limits

Set minimum and maximum values allowed for input.

Scale → Default Scale

Define a fallback scale when the referenced parameter is absent or unreadable.

Presence → Property / Condition

Choose whether the option is always offered, or offered when another Boolean property is true or false. This controls the configuration UI, not runtime visibility.

Preview

Preview the instance configuration pane. Changes made only in Preview do not persist as class defaults.

Limits & distinctions

Property type is distinct from Standard type. The Graphics expression description in the supplied type topic duplicates reference wording; use the installed help/editor to confirm that particular type.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ type : ValueType

The allowed value family. See the type catalog below: a Standard type, a variable type and a GEM option type are different catalogs.

+ defaultValue : Any

The starting/fallback value in this model. GEM class defaults are configured in the Designer; an unlinked GEM’s Designer does not define defaults.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ describe() : Metadata

Provide configuration metadata such as title, description and tooltip for an exposed option.

+ testPresence() : Boolean

Determine whether an option appears in the GEM configuration pane. Presence does not control the runtime graphic’s visibility.

+ validate(value : Any) : Boolean

Check a value against the option’s type and constraints. This summarizes a responsibility; no universal validate method is claimed.

A configured value for one exposed option on a GEM placement.

What can be created or contained?

Assign a compatible literal, reference, animation or expression where that option type permits it. This value is not a container for more graphic objects.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Configure the placed instance

OptionValue represents the value selected for a particular exposed GEM option. Select the placed GEM and edit the custom groups on Basics. The field names and availability are determined by the definition; the installed examples below are not a universal schema.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (5 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles on elements are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Linked to

References the GEM class to which this GEM is linked. (Appears only on linked GEMs.) Click the reference to open the GEM class as a document tab.

Created from

References the GEM class from which this GEM was created. (Appears only on unlinked GEMs.) Click the reference to open the GEM class as a document tab.

Version

Indicates what version of the GEM class this GEM instance is linked to. This property is read-only; Version is modified in the GEM class.

Basic Configuration (121 fields)
Abnormal State

Select the value (from 0 through 5 or None) that indicates an abnormal state for this device.

Alarm Function Block Name

Enter the name of the alarm function block to associate with this GEM.

Alarm Name

Enter the name of the alarm (such as HI_ALM or DV_LO_ALM) to use for the specified alarm type on this GEM.

Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Display Level

Select Level 1 to configure this GEM for Level 1 displays (the GEM does not show alarm icons or an alarm box). Select Level 2 to configure this GEM for Level 2 displays. (the GEM does show alarm icons and an alarm box).

Display Name

Enter the name of the display this button should open.

Chart Builder Configuration (3 fields)
Chart Builder

Select None to disable a context menu on this GEM. Select Default to use the default context menu options, which include SP, PV, and OUT. Select Custom to configure your own context menu options. You can add up to six menu options. If you selected to customize a context menu, configure the following properties:

Chart Builder → Parameter 1-6 Path

Chart Builder → Parameter 1-6 Description

Visibility (4 fields)
Visibility

Select Visible to keep the element visible and enable its configured online actions, if any. Select Hidden to hide the element and disable any configured online actions.

Blink

Select True to have the element blink on and off, according to the selected Blink Style . Select False to prevent the element from blinking.

Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Present Online

Select this check box to include all elements in the group or GEM when the graphics configuration is published online. The property provides a means to include a complex element on a contextual display (or display) during configuration, but to configure it to not consume resources when online.

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On unlinked GEMs only: To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's GEM Configuration Designer and Basics tab. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. You can modify the value of the new property on the Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

References: [133]

Limits & distinctions

A Display reference excludes contextual displays. Parameter/Scale references have specialized rules; many option types are not animate-able.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ definition : OptionDefinition

The option schema this value conforms to. The reference connects a value to its name, type and configuration metadata.

+ value : Any

The current or configured data carried by this item. Any is model shorthand here, not an assertion that every property accepts every type.

+ expression : Expression [0..1]

An optional expression supplying the configured value, where that property type supports expressions.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ resolve(context : Context) : Any

Obtain the effective value from the configured expression/reference or variant. The signature shows the relevant context, theme or language.

+ assign(value : Any)

Set the value where writable. Live variables backed by online parameters, standards or references cannot be assigned online as ordinary mutable variables.

Binding

Conceptual link from data/expression to a graphical property. It is not a literal Palette class.

What can be created or contained?

Configure static values, supported simple/blink/library animations, Standard references, variable references or GEM property references through property controls.

Property diamond menu

Binding is conceptual. Use the target property’s diamond for compatible Standard, variable, GEM-property references and animations. The excerpt below is the Display Basics diamond menu; other targets offer choices according to their type.

References: [97]

Limits & distinctions

The property type determines available choices. Evaluating appearance is separate from writing a process parameter.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ source : DataRef | Expression

Where a value comes from: a literal, a reference or an expression, as indicated in the signature. Reference-backed Live variables can be read-only online.

+ target : ElementProperty

The graphic/object property that receives the evaluated result, for example fill color, text or visibility.

+ conversion : FunctionRef [0..1]

An optional conversion between input data and the target property’s expected type. In Live this can reference a library function.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ readSource() : Any

Resolve the source data for a binding before conversion/evaluation.

+ evaluate() : Any

Compute the result of an expression or function from its inputs. This does not by itself imply changing controller data.

+ applyToTarget(value : Any)

Apply the resulting value to the destination graphical property.

Standard

A reusable value definition. Its type determines what value it holds and which properties can reference it.

What can be created or contained?

Choose one of the nine Standard types below. A particular Standard stores its value and applicable theme/language variations; it does not contain child Color/Font Standard instances.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Shared typed value

Select a Standard in Library Explorer. Basics configures its metadata, type-specific Value and Theme Values where applicable. A Standard does not have Display lifecycle tabs.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (3 fields)
Title

Enter a title for this standard. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Description

Enter additional information describing the standard (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Value

Select or enter a value for this standard. The options available depend on the standard type. Color standard — Select a color from the color gallery. Font standard — Select a font type, size, and style. Boolean standard — Select True or False. Image standard — Click the browse button to browse for and select an image. Click the drop-down arrow to copy the image or save it to another location. String standard — Enter the desired text. Private String standard — Enter the desired text. Multi-language String standard — Enter the desired text. Measurement standard — Select a measurement. Number standard — Select a number.

References: [32]

Standard types — 9 documented choices

These are alternative kinds of Standard, not nine child objects inside every Standard.

Color

A shared color value, such as a common outline or normal-state fill.

Font

A shared font family, size and style.

Boolean

A shared True/False value.

Image

A shared image asset/reference selected through the image browser.

String

Shared language-neutral text.

Private String

A specialized shared string used by documented application/query configuration. Follow the specific feature’s rules; it is not a secret-storage guarantee.

Multi-language String

Text with language-specific values.

Measurement

A shared linear measurement used by compatible graphical properties.

Number

A shared numeric value.

Limits & distinctions

Create under Library Explorer → Standards → Home/New, or via a compatible property’s diamond → New Standard. Publish changes to deploy them; referencing displays need not be republished just for a Standard value change.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ type : ValueType

The allowed value family. See the type catalog below: a Standard type, a variable type and a GEM option type are different catalogs.

+ variants : Variant [0..*]

Alternative values associated with the Standard, especially theme-specific values. Language variations depend on the string type.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ resolve(theme : Theme) : Any

Obtain the effective value from the configured expression/reference or variant. The signature shows the relevant context, theme or language.

+ resolve(language : Language) : Any

Obtain the effective value from the configured expression/reference or variant. The signature shows the relevant context, theme or language.

live · Documented concepts / model names

LibraryFunction

A reusable typed conversion from input values to a result suitable for a graphical property.

What can be created or contained?

Choose a result family below. Inside one function configure inputs (1–5), calculations (0–5), and Rule-Based, Value-Based or Script conversion logic.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Shared conversion

Select a Function in Library Explorer. Basics contains Information, Inputs, Calculations and Conversion Table. Rule-Based, Value-Based and Script are alternatives; a function is not a display-event handler.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a title for this function. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Description

Enter additional information describing this function (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Inputs (5 fields)
Add Input

Click to add an input for this function. You can add up to five inputs.

Add Input → Name

Enter a name for each input.

Add Input → Title

Enter a title for each input.

Add Input → Type

Select a type for each input (float, string, Boolean, or any). If you select Any , the input can be any of the three available types. Additionally, if you select Any , you cannot provide a default value because the input type is unknown.

Add Input → Default Value

Select the check box next to each input for which you want to provide a default value, and then enter or select a default value. If the check box is deselected (no default value provided), then when the function is referenced as an animation, the user is presented with a Edit Scripts/Browse field.

Calculations (1 fields)
Add Calculation

Click to add a calculation for this function. You can add up to five calculations. Enter a name for each calculation. Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant and write a script for this calculation. Or, click the browse button to browse for and reference items in the configuration libraries.

Conversion Table (12 fields)
Conversion Type

Select the type of conversion to use for this function (Rule–Based, Value–Based, or Script). Rule–based Value–based Script

Conversion Type → Add Rule

Click to add a conversion rule for this function.

Add Rule → Rule

Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant and write a script for this rule. Or, click the browse button to browse for and reference items in the configuration libraries.

Add Rule → Output

Select the output to show when the rule evaluates to true.

Conversion Type → Otherwise

Select the output to show when the rule evaluates to false.

Conversion Type → Evaluation Basis

Select the input to be evaluated. If this function has only one input, the evaluation basis has only one option.

Conversion Type → Add Value

Click to add a value for this function.

Add Value → Value

Enter a value or range of values to use in evaluating the input. Alternatively, click the Edit Scripts icon or browser.

Add Value → Output

Select the output to show when the conversion evaluates to true (the evaluation basis matches the conversion value). Alternatively, click the diamond to browse to or create a standard.

Conversion Type → Otherwise

Select the output to show when the conversion evaluates to false (the evaluation basis does not match the conversion value). Alternatively, click the diamond to browse to or create a standard.

Conversion Type → Status Exceptions

Select the color to use for each status exception (Unknown, Bad, and Uncertain). Alternatively, click the diamond next to each status exception to browse to or create a standard.

Conversion Type → Script

Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant and write the conversion logic for this function.

References: [33]

Function result families — 7 listed in the overview

Input types are separate: Float, String, Boolean, or Any in the detailed properties topic. Any accepts one of those three types and cannot have a default value.

Color

Returns a color, for example from status inputs.

Font

Returns a font selection for a compatible font property.

Boolean

Returns True/False.

Image

Returns an image result for a compatible property.

String

Returns text.

Measurement

Returns a graphical measurement.

Number

Returns a numeric result.

Inside a function

Inputs · 1–5

Named typed inputs; defaults are optional except Any cannot have a default. Inputs without defaults precede inputs with defaults.

Calculations · 0–5

Intermediate expressions using inputs or other calculations.

Rule-Based conversion

Rules select output values, with otherwise outputs.

Value-Based conversion

Compare an input/calculated value to choices or ranges; configure outputs, otherwise and relevant status exceptions.

Script conversion

Write the conversion logic in the supported function editor.

Limits & distinctions

Create under Library Explorer → Functions → Home/New. Color and Font functions are result families, not child objects nested inside another function. Function configuration is not an arbitrary external TypeScript module.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ inputs : FunctionInput [1..5]

One to five named function inputs. Input types and defaults are distinct from the function’s output family.

+ calculations : Calculation [0..5]

Zero to five intermediate expressions/calculations used before conversion. They can reference inputs and other calculations.

+ resultType : ValueType

The output family used by a compatible property: for example Color or Font. It is not the same as the input type.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ evaluate(inputs : Any[]) : Any

Compute the result of an expression or function from its inputs. This does not by itself imply changing controller data.

+ save()

Persist authoring changes. Saving and publishing/deploying are separate actions.

+ publish()

Deploy publishable configuration changes to Live. This is an editor/deployment responsibility, not a method on an SDK class.

Comparison gap

No native VBA UserForm equivalent is asserted in Live.

What can be created or contained?

A suitable runtime UI can be redesigned with contextual displays, GEMs and supported controls. Configure-time automation is a different requirement.

Actual editor / configuration surface

No native VBA UserForm class asserted

This comparison slot is intentionally empty on Live. Build suitable operator UI from supported documents and controls. A Configure-time automation form is a separate migration decision.

Limits & distinctions

Do not interpret this gap as proof that an arbitrary embedded form/control can be imported.

Template

Initial content for creating a new graphics configuration.

What can be created or contained?

Create Display, Contextual Display or Layout templates, from scratch or by saving an existing configuration as a template. Contents follow that configuration type.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Template editing follows its kind

A template supplies starting configuration for a Display, Contextual Display or Layout. Use the underlying kind’s editor; this is not ongoing inheritance and the template itself cannot be published or tested online.

References: [158] [159] [22]

Limits & distinctions

Templates cannot be published, tested online or referenced as runtime destinations. They do not create ongoing inheritance.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ kind : Display | Popup | Layout

The role or configuration family of the item, rather than an asserted native subclass enumeration.

+ initialContent : Configuration

The configuration copied when a new item is created from a template; later edits are not class inheritance.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ createNew(name : String)

Create a new display, contextual display or layout from starting content; not an instance that inherits future template changes.

+ editStartingContent()

Edit the starting content used for future copies/new items.
