Layout

Operator screen-space configuration and routing arrangement.

What can be created or contained?

Add Screens and DisplayFrames; use layout-supported elements, scoped variables and configured behavior. The Layout can come from a template.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select the layout root

Select the Layout to edit Basics, Interaction, Styling and Variables. Select a Screen or DisplayFrame child for that child’s own settings.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles on elements are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Background (1 fields)
Color

Select the background color for the layout.

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Pinning (1 fields)
Enable Contextual Display Pinning

Select this check box to enable pinning behavior on faceplates and detail displays. When this feature is enabled, a pushpin icon appears on contextual displays in DeltaV Live, giving the operator the option to keep contextual displays open when additional displays of that type are opened. Note : In Graphics Studio, you do not see the pushpin icons on contextual displays, even when Contextual Display Pinning is enabled.

Events (3 fields)
OnOpen

...when the layout opens.

OnClose

...when the layout closes.

OnKeyPress

. . . when a key is pressed.

Timers (7 fields)
Add Timer

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Add Timer → Name

Enter a name for the timer.

Add Timer → Title

Enter a title for the timer. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Add Timer → Description

Enter a description for the timer.

Add Timer → Script

Enter a custom script for the timer. (Click the Edit Scripts icon to open the Script Assistant.) For example, you can write a script that executes only once or a script that runs until a specified condition is met. See the Script Assistant for help on writing a custom script.

Add Timer → Active

Select True to enable this action for this timer. Select False to disable this action for this timer. When False is selected, actions of the same type, on any elements stacked behind this one, are not masked.

Add Timer → Duration

Select the duration (in milliseconds) of the interval between consecutive timer executions.

Variables (8 fields)
Add Variable

Click the drop-down arrow and select the type of variable you want to add. The variable is added to the Name/Type/Value table.

Name/Type/Value

Select a variable in the table to configure its properties. You can configure the following properties for each variable:

Name/Type/Value → Name

In the Name field, double-click the variable name to enter a new name for the variable. Names must be unique among the elements, GEM Configuration properties, and other variables contained by the group or GEM.

Name/Type/Value → Variable Properties

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Variable Properties → Title

Enter a title for the variable. A title may contain up to 64 characters.

Variable Properties → Description

Enter a description for the variable.

Variable Properties → Value

Enter or select a value for the variable. The value can be one of the following: Literal value Reference to a standard of a compatible type Simple or library animation Graphics expression

Variable Properties → OnWrite

Write a script for the behavior that is triggered when the value of this variable is updated online. Before that value is written to the variable, the OnWrite function verifies that the variable's new value is valid. (For more details on using the OnWrite function, refer to the topic, OnWrite function , in the Miscellaneous function section.)

Diamond context menu (32 fields)

The context menu may include some or all of the following options, depending on the property type:

Static Value

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Static Value → Set to Static Value

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Standards

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Standards → Browse for Standard

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Standards → New Standard

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

References

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

References → Variables

Select this option to reference a compatible variable existing on the containing graphics configuration.

References → GEM Configuration Properties

Select this option to reference a GEM configuration property. (Only custom properties can be selected.) This option appears on the context menu only on elements nested inside a GEM class or GEM (linked or unlinked). To reference an existing custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → < GEM property > . On GEM classes and unlinked GEMs only : To create and reference a new custom property, select GEM Configuration Properties → New Property . After selecting New Property , a new property of the type from which it was created is added to the unlinked GEM's or GEM class's GEM Configuration Designer. Additionally, the property field automatically populates a reference to the new property. On GEM classes, you can modify the default value of the new property in the GEM Configuration Designer . On unlinked GEMs, you can modify the value of the new property in the GEM's Basics tab.

References → Browse for Reference

Select this option to reference a variable existing on the containing display or GEM class, or on any GEMs or groups on the display or GEM class.

GEM Overrides

This section appears on the context menu only when this element is nested inside a linked GEM.

GEM Overrides → Override

Select this option to create an override on this property. When the property is overridden, it stops tracking the GEM class's value for this property and uses the override value instead. When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

GEM Overrides → Remove Override

Select this option to remove the override on this property. When the override is removed, the property once again tracks the GEM class value.

References: [122]

Limits & distinctions

Published layouts are assigned through Workstation Management; only one layout is assigned to a workstation/session at a time.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ screens : Screen [0..*]

Screen elements that define the layout’s monitor-space arrangement. Each Screen can own display frames.

+ workstation : Assignment [0..*]

Workstation/session assignment responsibility. Assignment is managed through Workstation Management, not as a claimed Layout API field.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ arrangeScreens()

Configure Screen elements in the Layout to represent the intended operator display space.

+ configureRouting()

Set display-frame routing/coordination rules. The saved document tree is separate from the navigation hierarchy.

+ publish()

Deploy publishable configuration changes to Live. This is an editor/deployment responsibility, not a method on an SDK class.

DisplaySet

Collection and navigation organization of Display references.

What can be created or contained?

Add hierarchical/non-hierarchical references and placeholders for future displays. A set can have several hierarchies, at most four levels deep.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Membership is separate from Basics

DisplaySet Basics holds Title and Description. Arrange display references and their levels in the display-set hierarchy editor; those memberships are not graphic children on a display canvas.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a title for the display set (optional).

Description

Enter additional information describing the display set (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

References: [106]

Limits & distinctions

The same display can occur once per set and in multiple sets at different levels. These are references, not owned graphic copies.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ references : DisplayReference [0..*]

Membership references to saved displays. A display set does not own copies of their graphical content.

+ hierarchies : Hierarchy [0..*]

Navigation groupings of display references, up to four levels deep in the supplied help. One set can contain several hierarchies.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ addDisplay(display : Display)

Add a reference to a saved display into a display set; do not copy its graphic tree.

+ assignLevel(level : Integer)

Place a display reference within a set’s hierarchy. The supported hierarchy is at most four levels deep.

+ navigate(ref : DisplayReference)

Select a referenced display through the navigation arrangement; destination routing depends on Layout/DisplayFrame configuration.

Screen

Layout element representing physical monitor space.

What can be created or contained?

Add DisplayFrame regions to arrange the screen. Screens are contained by a Layout.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select a screen in a layout

Basics sets the monitor representation and fallback target frame. Menu Bar configures the screen menu. Select a DisplayFrame child for frame routing and styling.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Screen Properties (5 fields)
Screen Size

Select the screen size, which represents the size and relative position of an operator's physical monitor. Each option shows the size in aspect ratio and world units. To configure a custom screen size, select Custom . Then, configure the following properties:

Screen Size → Diagonal Size

Select the screen size from a bottom corner to a top corner. Changing the Diagonal Size also changes the Width and Height.

Screen Size → Aspect Ratio

Select the screen's aspect ratio (horizontal : vertical). Changing the Aspect Ratio also changes the Width and Height.

Screen Size → Width

Select the width of the screen. Changing the Width also changes the Diagonal Size and Aspect Ratio.

Screen Size → Height

Select the Height of the screen. Changing the Height also changes the Diagonal Size and Aspect Ratio.

Display Frame (1 fields)

Select a target display frame for this screen. The target display frame is used as a fallback behavior when a display opened from a menu bar does not have a display frame designated for its hierarchy level. Important : Emerson recommends defining a target display frame for each screen, so that if a display opened from a menu bar does not have a designated home in the layout (through the Auto-open Display Levels property), the display will still open in a display frame. If you do not select a target display frame, then displays of this type open as popups.

Target Display Frame

Select a target display frame from the drop-down list.

DisplayFrame

Region of a Screen that presents displays according to routing/coordination settings.

What can be created or contained?

Configure routing rules and an optional navigation bar. A displayed document is presented/referenced, not copied into the frame’s saved element tree.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select a display frame

Basics configures routing, initial display, navigation and geometry. Styling configures frame presentation. A frame presents a saved display; it does not copy or own that display’s definition.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (2 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. Titles on elements are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Display frame (5 fields)
Frame Type

Define whether displays other than the initial display can open in this frame. Select Dynamic to allow other displays to open and replace the initial display in this frame. Select Static to prevent displays from opening and replacing the initial display in this frame.

Initial Display

Define the display that opens automatically in this display frame when DeltaV Live opens, when you click the Home button, or when you reset the layout. You can use this property to define the permanent displays that should appear in the layout, such as the Alarm Banner display. Home button and Reset layout Select Named Display to specify the initial display by name. Select Position in Hierarchy to specify the initial display by its position in the display set's hierarchy.

Initial Display → Display

If you selected Named Display for the initial display, enter or browse to the name of the display you want to use.

Initial Display → Position

If you selected Position in Hierarchy for the initial display, define the position in the display set's hierarchy that you want to use for the initial display. L1: Select the position of the overview display under which the desired initial display resides. L2: Select the position of the Level 2 display under which the desired initial display resides. L3: Select the position of the Level 3 display under which the desired initial display resides. L4: Select the position of the Level 4 display under which the desired initial display resides. Figure 1 shows an example of a display frame that is configured to open, as the initial display, the second Level 4 display under the fifth Level 3 display, which is under the third Level 2 display, which is under the first Overview display. Figure 2 shows the display that is in the position indicated by this display frame configuration. Display frame configuration for specifying an initial display according to its position in the display set's hierarchy Display set hierarchy

Target Display Frame

Main displays opened from a static frame open in the specified Target Display Frame. (Contextual displays opened from static frames still open as pop-ups.) If you selected Static for the Frame Type, enter the name of the display frame in which the display will open. Tip : For more information on the various ways that main displays can be opened from a display frame, see the topic, Configuring how users can open main displays in DeltaV Live . For more information on configuring where displays open in a layout, see the topic, Configuring where displays open in a layout .

Navigation Bar (10 fields)

Tip : Enabling a navigation bar on multiple display frames provides further flexibility in relocating displays.

Enable Navigation Bar

Click this check box to show the navigation bar at the top of this display frame. If you enable the navigation bar, configure the following properties:

Enable Navigation Bar → Navigation Source

Define how the display call-up buttons appear in the navigation bar. Select Flat List to show the display buttons in a vertical list that does not show the display set hierarchy. Select Display Hierarchy to show the display call-up buttons according to their display set hierarchy. If you select Display Hierarchy as the navigation source, configure the following properties for the display call-up buttons: Note : If a workstation does not have an active display set when the Navigation Source is set to Display Hierarchy , then the display call-up buttons default to a flat list.

Navigation Source → Highest Level to show

Select the highest display hierarchy level that should appear on a display call-up button. For example, if you select 2 as the highest level to show, then Level 2 is the highest level of displays that will appear on a display call-up button.

Navigation Source → Number of Levels to show

Select the highest display level to show in each call-up button's drop-down list. For example, if you select 3 as the number of levels to show, then each call-up button’s drop-down list will show all nested displays up to Level 3.

Navigation Source → Style

Choose which display levels appear as their own display call-up buttons. Displays at the level of the Highest Level to show always appear in the first (top) row. Select Single Row if you want call-up buttons for only displays at the Highest Level to show . These buttons appear in a single row. Select Double Row if you want call-up buttons for displays at both the Highest Level to show and the next level. Call-up buttons for displays at the next level appear in the second row. Select Triple Row if you want call-up buttons for displays at the Highest Level to show and the next two levels. Call-up buttons for displays at the next level appear in the third row.

Navigation Source → Show Alarm Rollup

Configure an alarm rollup to show next to each display button on the navigation bar. The alarm rollup shows active alarms in modules, devices, and nodes from both the parent display and its child displays. Select No Rollup if you do not want to show an alarm rollup. Select Primary Control Display to count alarms associated with the primary control display. Select Plant Hierarchy to count alarms associated with that display's configured Plant Hierarchy (area, unit, or equipment module).

Show Alarm Rollup → Alarm Rollup Filter

Select whether to include all active alarms in the alarm rollup or to apply the same filters as in the Alarm Banner.

Enable Navigation Bar → Enable Display History Buttons

Select this check box to show arrow buttons that allow you to navigate between displays. The forward and backward arrows let you navigate between previously-opened displays, and the up arrow lets you navigate to the current display's parent display. Display history buttons apply only to the display frame containing the navigation bar.

Enable Navigation Bar → Enable Display Relocation Button

Select this check box to show the Display Relocation button on the navigation bar. The operator can use this button to open a display as a new window, swap the position of two displays, or copy a display to another display frame. This button applies only to displays already open in a display frame. Note : Emerson recommends that you disable the display relocation button if you are using automatic display coordination. In other words, if you enable this option (check box is checked), you should also select the Prevent External Coordination check box in the Automatic Display Coordination property group.

Enable Navigation Bar → Show Home Button

Select this check box to show a home button on the navigation bar. The home button returns this display frame to the configured initial display.

Automatic Display Coordination (8 fields)
Auto-Coordinate Higher Levels

Select this check box to allow displays that are hierarchically related to each other appear together in the layout. When this option is enabled, and a display opens in this display frame, its parent opens in another display frame. When this option is disabled, parent displays do not open in other display frames. If Auto-open Display Levels is enabled, parent displays open in the display frame designated for that level. If Auto-open Display Levels is not enabled, parent displays open as 'other displays.'

Prevent External Coordination

Select this check box to prevent external coordination with other display frames. When external coordination is disabled on a display frame (check box is unchecked), opening a display from this frame's navigation bar opens that display in a different display frame. When external coordination is prevented on a display frame (check box is checked), opening a display from this frame's navigation bar opens that display only in a this display frame. Displays are prevented from opening in any other frame. Tip : Emerson recommends that you disable Display Relocation if you are using automatic display coordination. In other words, if you enable Display Relocation , you should also select the Prevent External Coordination check box.

Auto-open Display Levels

Select this check box to automatically open displays, in this display frame, that are of the same level as the level specified below.

Auto-open Display Levels → Overview Displays

Select this check box to designate this display frame to open only overview displays (displays in the overview position of a display set's navigation hierarchy).

Auto-open Display Levels → Level 2

Select this check box to designate this display frame to open only Level 2 displays (displays in the Level 2 position of a display set's navigation hierarchy).

Auto-open Display Levels → Level 3

Select this check box to designate this display frame to open only Level 3 displays (displays in the Level 3 position of a display set's navigation hierarchy).

Auto-open Display Levels → Level 4

Select this check box to designate this display frame to open only Level 4displays (displays in the Level 4 position of a display set's navigation hierarchy).

Auto-open Display Levels → Other Displays

Select this check box to designate this display frame to open any non-hierarchical displays in the active display set or any displays not contained in the active display set but available on this workstation.

Geometry (5 fields)
Width

Select the width for the element.

Height

Select the height for the element.

Lock Aspect Ratio

The supplied help contains only a placeholder or incomplete description for this field (Placeholder). Its precise behavior is not established here; check the installed editor/help rather than inferring it from the name.

Horizontal Position

Select the horizontal distance from the left side of the display to the element's center point (point of rotation).

Vertical Position

Select the vertical distance from the top of the display to the element's center point (point of rotation).

This menu option is available on a property that is already configured as an animation or reference. Select this option to remove the animation or reference and return the property to a static value.

Animations

The supplied help lists this field without a description. Its behavior is not established by this topic; inspect the installed editor/help.

Animations → Animation

Select this option to create a simple animation for this property type. Simple animations can be created on Boolean, percent, measurement, degree, and font property types. For this type of animation, configure any of the following properties that apply to that property type:

Animation → Value / Fill

Enter the expression that resolves to the DeltaV parameter value to be animated.

Animation → Default value

Select the value to use when the animation logic is unable to resolve to a usable dynamic value.

Animation → Scale

Enter the path that resolves to the desired scaling parameter.

Scale → Default Scale

Enter the upper and lower scale values, engineering units, and number of decimals for the default scale. The default scale is used if the expression cannot be resolved.

Animation → Fill behavior

Select how you want the fill to behave on the element. 0% to Fill% : Fills the element from the bottom of the element to the default fill percent. Fill% to 100% : Fills the element from the default fill percent to the top of the element. Fill1% to Fill2% : Fills the element from Fill value 1 to Fill value 2.

Animation → Start Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 0% of Scale.

Animation → End Point

Enter the measurement to be used when the value is at 100% of Scale.

Animation → Degree Bounds

Enter the degrees boundaries for the fill color.

Animation → Direction

Select whether you want the fill to move clockwise or counterclockwise.

Animation → Alternate Font

Select the font to use when the alternate font condition is true.

Animation → Alternate Font Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the text uses the alternate font. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default font is used.

Animations → Blink Animation

Select this option to create a blink animation on a color property. Configure the following properties:

Blink Animation → Alternating Color Condition

Enter an expression that defines the condition under which the blinking behavior occurs. When the condition is true, the color alternates between the On Color and Off Color. When the expression is false or unresolvable, the default color is used.

Blink Animation → On Color

Select the color to use during the 'on time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Off Color

Select the color to use during the 'off time' duration of the blink style cycle.

Blink Animation → Blink Style

Choose whether you want the element to use the Standard Blink Rate or the Alternate Blink Rate . The blink rate for each blink style is defined in a Layout's Styling tab. The default for a standard blink rate is 500 milliseconds. The default for an alternate blink rate is 125 milliseconds.

Blink Animation → Default Color

Select the color to use when the alternating color condition is false or unresolvable.

Animations → Library Animation

Select this option to reference a library function of this property type. When you reference a library function, additional properties appear that let you override the default value ( Default property value ) and sometimes the input value ( Value ) in the referenced function. These override values apply only to that property on that element.

Select this option to reference an existing standard value. After selecting this option, use the browser window to browse to the desired library and standard.

Select this option to create a new standard of the same type. You can then reference the new standard from the Diamond context menu.

GEM Overrides → Override

When you create an override from the context menu, the value does not automatically change. You can still modify the value here or on the Overrides tab.

Limits & distinctions

If no frame matches the display’s hierarchy/other-display routing, the display can open in a popup.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ bounds : Geometry

The position and size of the display region, not the dimensions of every document shown within it.

+ routing : RoutingRules

Rules selecting which levels or other displays open in the frame and how related frames coordinate.

+ currentDisplay : Display [0..1]

An optional runtime display being presented. This is runtime state, not a new ownership link to the saved definition.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ selectDisplay(reference : DisplayRef)

Choose the display to be presented in a frame, as determined by navigation/routing.

+ present(display : Display)

Show a display in the frame. Presentation is not ownership of the saved display definition.

Display

Saved process graphic presented in a display frame or popup window.

What can be created or contained?

Add eligible graphic elements, groups, GEM instances, variables and interactions. Membership in display sets is configured separately.

Actual editor / configuration surface

Select the display itself

Select the Display root in Selection or clear the element selection on its canvas. Graphics Configuration should identify DISPLAY, as in your screenshot. Basics, Interaction and Variables belong to the document; selecting a button changes the pane to that button’s tabs.

Basics

Documented editor fields. Hover or focus a field; click it for the full supplied explanation.

Information (5 fields)
Title

Enter a friendly name for the element (optional). A title may contain up to 64 characters. If a display has a title, the display title is used online. If a display does not have a title, the display name is used online.

Description

Enter additional information describing the element (optional). Descriptions are visible only in Graphics Studio.

Plant Hierarchy

If you want this display to participate in alarm rollup behavior on a navigation bar, enter the name of the DeltaV area, unit, or equipment module for which you want to show alarms on this display. The alarm rollup shows all active or unacknowledged alarms in modules, devices, and nodes from both the parent display and its child displays, according to the display set hierarchy. If you do not want this display to participate in alarm rollup behavior, leave this field blank.

Supporting Display

Select this check box to omit this display from the drop-down list on DeltaV Live display call-up buttons.

Allow Debugging

Select this check box to enable the DeltaV Live debugger on this display. When enabled, you can see the source code, set breakpoints, and step through the code on this display in DeltaV Live. Attention : Enabling this feature may affect the loading time for this display.

Size (4 fields)

Customize the size of this display either by configuring a width and height for the display or by configuring the display size to match the size of a specific display frame.

Width

Select a width for this display.

Height

Select a height for this display.

Fit to Display Frame

In the drop-down list, select the display frame to which you want to match the size of this display. (The layout configuration determines the display frame in which this display opens.) Note : Fitting the display to a display frame will override the configurations in the Width and Height properties. If you want to use the Width and Height selections, do not select a display frame for this property.

Lock Aspect Ratio

Select the check box to keep the width and height of the display size proportional.

Background (1 fields)
Color

Select the background color for the display.

View (2 fields)

Tip : You can control the position of the viewport through scripting with Dsp.Scroll().

View Type

Configure the zoom at which this display opens when it is first opened in an instance of DeltaV Live. Note : Configuring a view type does not change the actual size of the display. For example, if the display is sized to fit a display frame and the display opens in a display frame other than for which it is sized, then the display size remains the same, while the display is scaled to fit the configured view type. The configured view type typically applies only the first time the display is opened in an instance of Delta Live. If that display is called a second time, it preserves its original viewport. However, note the different behavior for the view type in the following scenarios: If the operator did not execute any other zooming or panning on a display while it was previously opened, then the configured view type is preserved. If a display is open in multiple display frames at the same time, the viewport state persists for the last display frame to zoom or pan. Scale to Display Frame (default selection) - The display is scaled to fit the display frame in which it opens. Fit Height - When the display opens, it is scaled up or down to fit the height of the display frame in which it opens. If the display is larger than the display frame allows, the display will have horizontal scroll bars so that the operator can navigate to any part of the display. Fit Width - When the display opens, it is scaled up or down to fit the width of the display frame in which it opens. If the display is larger than the display frame allows, the display will have vertical scroll bars so that the operator can navigate to any part of the display. Custom View - The display opens scaled to the user-configured percentage in Zoom % . If the display is larger than the display frame allows, the display will have horizontal and vertical scroll bars so that the operator can navigate to any part of the display.

View Type → Zoom %

Select the zoom percentage (50%-400%) at which the display will open within the display frame.

Variable Properties → OnWrite

Limits & distinctions

A display can belong to multiple sets. Display level belongs to its position in each set, not to group/GEM nesting.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ elements : GraphicElement [0..*]

Graphic content owned by this document. Groups and GEMs can introduce additional levels of containment.

+ navigationRole : SetMembership [0..*]

The display’s membership/position in display sets. Its level can differ between sets.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ open()

Open the configured document at runtime, optionally with context. Real API selection and arguments are covered in Section 5.

+ close()

Close the runtime document/UI. Closing does not delete its saved definition.

+ publish()

Deploy publishable configuration changes to Live. This is an editor/deployment responsibility, not a method on an SDK class.

Place the source dynamo into a picture. Associated forms/code may copy; external dependencies may not.

+ saveSource()

Save edits to the source asset. How existing copies are updated must be determined from the site’s actual tooling.

GraphicObject

Conceptual common category for actual Operate graphics.

What can be created or contained?

Specific object/control types must be inventoried in Configure. There is no assertion that every control can be nested in every container.

Actual editor / configuration surface

The Operate model describes responsibilities, not a verified list of native property tabs. Use the installed Operate property dialogs, VBA object browser and the actual custom form/code for exact members. Live tabs are not copied onto these illustrative counterparts.

Limits & distinctions

Operate internals and custom behavior are illustrative here. Confirm specific object/control capabilities in the installed help and actual VBA project.

Attributes · compact conceptual model

+ name : String

Identifier for this configuration item or model object. Naming scopes differ: library item names are local to their configuration library.

+ geometry : Geometry

Position, size and applicable transformation values. Supported geometry properties depend on the element type.

+ bindings : Binding [0..*]

The data references, expressions or animations that supply this graphic’s property values. Binding is an explanatory category.

Operations · conceptual responsibilities

+ evaluateAppearance()

Resolve data/expressions into visible property values. This is evaluation, not a click-event sequence.

+ dispatch(event : Event)

Route an event to the configured behavior, where supported by the element.

+ render()

Present the resolved graphical appearance. This models a runtime responsibility, not a user-callable render function.

Relationship scope & platform differences
  • GraphicDocument → GraphicElement: an element has one immediate owner; document and group ownership are alternatives ({xor}). GEM content supplies other valid ownership paths. Popup containment is inherited through the conceptual document category.
  • GEM instance → GEM class: linked instances retain a class reference; an unlinked instance has none. The attribute type describes configuration reuse, not inheritance between GEM classes. Eligible overrides and nested links follow Section 2.
  • Source dynamo → placed dynamo: placement creates graphic content. The dashed arrow does not promise Live-style linked propagation. Inspect the site's update code separately.
  • Options: Live has a defined schema/instance distinction. Operate FormOption and ConfiguredValue are illustrative responsibilities of custom VBA, not a universal native object model. Presence and runtime visibility remain different; see Section 3.
  • Variables and bindings: scopes differ by owner. The event-to-variable dependency means code can use state; it does not mean the event handler owns all variables. assign() on a Live variable is constrained by its source and writability.
  • Template / starter picture: creates initial content for a new document. They do not provide ongoing class inheritance. That cross-band creation dependency is omitted from the drawing to keep its long reference lines readable.
  • Screen routing: Layout owns Screens, Screens own DisplayFrames; DisplaySets reference Displays independently. Display and ContextualDisplay are conceptual GraphicDocument specializations; the long Display-to-GraphicDocument generalization is omitted. Operate picture roles similarly are not asserted native subclasses. See Section 6.
  • UserForms: Operate form events can manipulate graphics or runtime data according to their code. No drop-in Live UserForm or general Configure-time scripting host is implied by the blank slot.
  • Model boundary: supporting value types, editors, controllers, deployment services, ActiveX dependencies, individual leaf controls and every API overload are not expanded. This is a consolidated class view of the reference's graphics scope, not an exhaustive reverse-engineered DeltaV implementation.

Numbered references open this index. Each entry links to the supplied help topic or UML resource and back to its cited passages. Live relationships are checked against that help; Operate custom-code paths are explicitly illustrative. These models do not establish private implementation classes or a universal API across v14, v15 and v16.

All diagrams are embedded. SVG buttons save the embedded diagram. Local help links resolve on this machine.
